children: BTCUSD spot CFD saw a sharp derivatives correction, triggering about $859 million in long liquidations—roughly 86% of total liquidations—concentrating forced unwinds among long holders.
BTCUSD rose ~35% from August lows to about $83k–$84k by late September; gains driven by spot demand, ETF inflows and short covering; futures leverage showed no similar increase.
A 17,733 BTC on-chain transfer (~$1.484B) moved to Coinbase Prime amid rising selling pressure in Bitcoin vs US Dollar, Spot CFD (BTCUSD).
BTCUSD traded near $82,900, close to average holder break-even ~$80,500. A weekly close above $82,700 signals buyer control; upside targets noted around $87,000–$88,000.
BTCUSD remains driven by derivatives, especially high-leverage perpetual futures, which fuel short-term price swings; risk-detection tools improved, but heavy leverage still shapes BTCUSD moves.
Analyst says BTCUSD mirrors late‑2025/early‑2026 pattern, trading near investors' capital‑weighted cost basis and oscillating around that aggregated cost level rather than trending decisively.
BTCUSD spot: ETFs hold 1.48M BTC, firms 1.66M, governments ~518.5k, individuals ~13.9M (≈66% supply). Institutions net bought in 2025; individuals net sold.
Morgan Stanley’s MSBT bought ~92 BTC this week, raising its Bitcoin vs US Dollar Spot CFD (BTCUSD) position to about 10,639 BTC (~$880M), per Arkham data on recent accumulation.
